answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an economy of AI agents anchors identity to a decentralized trust atlas governed by cryptographically staked bonds. A graph kernel calculates structural trust scores across the network by evaluating transaction volume and compute output variations. Creating fake identities requires an attacker to lock non-refundable collateral for every synthesized edge; because the marginal cost grows quadratically with each network delta, scaling Sybil nodes becomes prohibitively expensive.
